name: AI-Augmented Regulatory Change Management
summary: Regulatory updates are captured and pre-screened by agents so specialists only review applicable or uncertain items. An Impact Assessment Agent drafts the assessment and SMEs confirm through structured tasks; a Risk Classification Agent proposes the ICH Q9 category and the QA Manager decides. The Change Request is created automatically, pre-checked for compliance gaps, and approved by humans through a 48-hour asynchronous CCB vote with Part 11 signatures for High risk. Agents draft document redlines and compile the closure evidence, while document owners, QA and the QA Analyst retain every approval.

nodes.name: Regulatory update published
nodes.description: A new or revised regulation, guidance or monograph appears in a monitored source.

nodes.name: Regulatory Intake Agent
nodes.description: Monitors FDA, EMA, ICH and pharmacopoeial sources, de-duplicates items, extracts metadata and writes the RIL entry and archive within hours of publication.

nodes.name: Applicability Screening Agent
nodes.description: Reads the full document, matches scope against products, sites, registrations and systems, and proposes Applicable / Not Applicable with rationale, confidence and a draft Regulatory Summary.

nodes.name: Applicability outcome
nodes.description: Routes on the agent's proposed outcome and confidence against the 0.85 threshold.

nodes.name: RA Specialist applicability review
nodes.description: Reviews the agent's rationale and evidence, confirms or overturns applicability and finalises the Regulatory Summary. Decision recorded in the RIL with the reviewer's identity.

nodes.name: RA Manager batch countersign
nodes.description: Weekly review and countersignature of high-confidence Not Applicable determinations from a single queue, replacing per-item e-mail approvals.

nodes.name: Impact Assessment Agent
nodes.description: Semantically matches the change to SOPs, batch records, specifications, validation documents, registrations and curricula; drafts FRM-QA-042-01 and generates targeted confirm/adjust tasks per SME.

nodes.name: SME impact confirmation
nodes.description: SMEs confirm or adjust pre-identified impacts and effort estimates via structured tasks with a 2-day SLA; the QA Analyst resolves conflicts and finalises the IA.

nodes.name: Risk Classification Agent
nodes.description: Maps the IA against the SOP's Low / Medium / High criteria (registered details, CQAs, CPPs, data integrity, submission need) and drafts a rationale and recommended approval pathway.

nodes.name: QA Manager risk sign-off
nodes.description: Confirms or changes the proposed classification from a prioritised approval queue. Proposed HIGH or confidence below 0.85 also notifies the Head of Quality.

nodes.name: Auto-create Change Request
nodes.description: Populates all 14 eQMS fields from the IA, Regulatory Summary and risk classification, attaches source documents and drafts the action plan; the Process Owner reviews and submits.

nodes.name: Compliance Pre-Review Agent
nodes.description: Checks the CR against the regulatory text, policy library and ALCOA+ checklist, flags gaps to the Process Owner and drafts a filing-impact note.

nodes.name: Compliance & RA review
nodes.description: Compliance Officer confirms the compliance position; RA Manager decides the filing strategy. Agent flags with confidence below 0.85 are highlighted for attention.

nodes.name: Risk level
nodes.description: Selects the approval pathway defined in SOP 6.4.3.

nodes.name: Low-risk e-approval
nodes.description: Electronic approval by the Process Owner and QA Manager without CCB presentation, as permitted by SOP 6.7.4.

nodes.name: CCB asynchronous e-vote
nodes.description: CCB members approve, reject or return the CR by e-vote in the eQMS within 48 hours, using an AI-assembled briefing pack that has passed completeness checks. Any member can call a synchronous meeting.

nodes.name: Part 11 dual signature
nodes.actor: Head of Quality and Site Head
nodes.description: Electronic signatures for High risk changes in accordance with 21 CFR Part 11. Never delegated to AI or automation.

nodes.name: Documentation Drafting Agent
nodes.description: Generates first-pass redlines for each affected controlled document, validates numbering, cross-references and citations, and prepares approval routing per the document approval matrix.

nodes.name: Document owner & QA approval
nodes.description: Owners edit and approve redlines; QA and functional heads approve in the DMS. Document Control confirms formatting on exception only.

nodes.name: Issuance, training assignment & tracking
nodes.description: Sets the effective date (30 days after approval, retained as a policy control), archives superseded versions, assigns training from the curriculum matrix, sends reminders and raises the 95% completion escalation. Instructor-led sessions for High risk remain human-delivered.

nodes.name: Verification & Audit Agent
nodes.description: Cross-checks eQMS, DMS, LMS and the submissions tracker, compiles a closure package with evidence links, and schedules the 90-day effectiveness check for High risk changes.

nodes.name: QA closure sign-off
nodes.description: Reviews the closure package, resolves any failed check and closes the CR; the RIL is updated automatically.

nodes.name: Change closed
nodes.description: Change Request closed with a complete, attributable audit trail.

agents.name: Regulatory Intake Agent
agents.purpose: Continuously monitor designated regulatory sources and log every potentially relevant update with structured metadata, so no applicable change is missed and specialists stop reading feeds.
inputs: FDA Federal Register and guidance pages
outputs: RIL entry (source, date, title, URL, type, authority, topics)
permissions: Read public regulatory sources
Create RIL entries
Store source documents in the RA archive
prohibited_actions: Edit or delete existing RIL entries
Send notifications outside the RA team
agents.escalation_conditions: Document type cannot be classified with confidence ≥ 0.80, a monitored source is unreachable for more than 24 hours, or weekly volume deviates by more than 50% from baseline.

agents.name: Applicability Screening Agent
agents.purpose: Determine whether a regulatory update affects the company's products, processes, sites, registrations or systems, and prepare the evidence a specialist needs to decide quickly.
outputs: Proposed Applicable / Not Applicable with confidence
permissions: Read source documents and inventories
Write proposed outcome and rationale to the RIL as a draft
Route items to the RA Specialist queue
agents.escalation_conditions: Confidence < 0.85, proposed outcome is Applicable, or the update references a registered product, a critical process parameter or a data-integrity requirement — route to the RA Specialist.

agents.name: Impact Assessment Agent
agents.purpose: Identify every SOP, record, specification, validation document, registration and training curriculum affected by an applicable change, and turn SME research into a confirmation task.
tools: Semantic search across DMS and eQMS
permissions: Read DMS, eQMS, inventories and curricula
Draft the IA form
Create and remind SME tasks
agents.escalation_conditions: Any affected-document match below 0.85 confidence, an SME disagrees with the draft, or no SME response within 2 business days — escalate to the QA Analyst and the functional manager.

agents.name: Risk Classification Agent
agents.purpose: Propose the ICH Q9-based risk classification and approval pathway with a transparent rationale so the QA Manager can decide from a prioritised queue.
permissions: Read the IA and reference data
Write a proposed classification as a draft
Notify the QA Manager and, for HIGH, the Head of Quality
prohibited_actions: Set or change the final risk classification
Downgrade a classification previously set by a human
agents.escalation_conditions: Always requires QA Manager confirmation. Proposed HIGH or confidence < 0.85 additionally notifies the Head of Quality.

agents.name: Compliance Pre-Review Agent
agents.purpose: Catch interpretation, policy, data-integrity and completeness gaps before the Change Request reaches Compliance and Regulatory reviewers, so the formal review needs one cycle.
outputs: Gap list with severity and evidence
permissions: Read the CR, policies and regulatory text
Post pre-review comments to the CR
Draft the filing-impact note
prohibited_actions: Approve or clear the compliance review
agents.escalation_conditions: All output is reviewed by the Compliance Officer; flags with confidence < 0.85 are highlighted. Any potential submission requirement escalates to the RA Manager.

agents.name: Documentation Drafting Agent
agents.purpose: Produce consistent first-pass redlines for every affected controlled document and eliminate cross-reference, numbering and citation errors before human review.
inputs: Approved Change Request and action plan
Current controlled documents from the DMS
outputs: Proposed approval routing per the approval matrix
permissions: Read controlled documents
Create draft revisions in the DMS draft workspace
Propose approval routing
prohibited_actions: Approve, issue or make effective any controlled document
Change validated-system procedures without Document Control review
agents.escalation_conditions: Insertion point cannot be located with confidence ≥ 0.85, the change touches a validated-system procedure, or the document owner rejects the redline — escalate to the Document Control Specialist.

agents.name: Verification & Audit Agent
agents.purpose: Verify that every implementation action is complete across systems and assemble an attributable closure package, so QA closes changes on evidence rather than manual cross-checking.
outputs: Verification checklist with pass/fail per control
permissions: Read eQMS, DMS, LMS and submissions tracker
Compile and attach the closure package
Schedule effectiveness checks
agents.escalation_conditions: Any verification control fails or evidence is missing — escalate to the QA Analyst; repeated failures escalate to the QA Manager.

agents.name: Change Workflow Automation
agents.purpose: Deterministic, rule-based data movement and scheduling between the RIL, eQMS, DMS and LMS. Not an AI agent: no judgement, fully auditable rules.
outputs: Training assignments, reminders and escalation notices
permissions: Create CR drafts
Set effective dates on approved documents
Assign training and send reminders
prohibited_actions: Submit or approve a Change Request
agents.escalation_conditions: Any mandatory field cannot be populated, an API validation fails, or training completion is below 95% five days before the effective date.

expected_improvements: End-to-end cycle (publication → CR closure, excluding the 30-day training window): ~48 → ~14 business days
Hands-on human effort per applicable change: ~41 → ~9 hours
Regulatory screening: ~13 hours/week of manual reading replaced by automated intake; specialists review only applicable or low-confidence items (~8-15% of volume)
Impact assessment: 7-12 days of e-mail coordination → 2-3 days of structured SME confirmation
CCB wait: 4.5 days plus 20% re-presentation → 48-hour asynchronous e-vote on completeness-checked packs
Change Request creation: ~60% duplicate data entry eliminated
Human-to-human handoffs: 8 → 4; agents carry context between steps
Documentation quality: automated cross-reference and citation checks before human review (target 1.4 → <0.5 errors per document set)
governance_controls: Explainability: every agent output carries a rationale, confidence score and SOP/regulation citations; nothing is presented as a bare decision.

Human oversight: 10 human approval gates remain (applicability, SME confirmation, risk sign-off, compliance review, CCB vote, Part 11 signatures, document approval, closure); no AI node connects directly to an execution node without one.
Auditability: all agent actions, human decisions, reviewer identities, timestamps and comments are written to an append-only audit trail aligned with 21 CFR Part 11 audit-trail expectations.
Permission boundaries: agents hold least-privilege access — read broadly, write drafts only; prohibited actions are enforced at the tool layer, not just in prompts.
Escalation rules: a 0.85 confidence threshold (0.90 for verification) routes work to a named human role; any HIGH risk classification forces human approval before execution.
